key_findings.finding: The key—and apparently only direct—primary IDCM study is PMID 27496484, “BRCA1 Reflects Myocardial Adverse Remodeling in Idiopathic Dilated Cardiomyopathy” (Transplantation Proceedings, 2016). It was a case-control myocardial immunohistochemistry study: explanted hearts from 10 men with IDCM undergoing transplantation (mean age 44±5.3 years, no clinical ischemic heart disease) versus myocardial fragments from 10 male cerebral-death valve/pulmonary-artery donors (40±2.3 years).

In that study, BRCA1 was detected with a rabbit polyclonal antibody and semiquantitatively scored in cardiocytes, small vessels/capillaries, and interstitial cells. All IDCM samples were positive and showed mosaic/nonuniform staining: hypertrophied cardiocytes stained very intensely, whereas typical cardiomyopathic cardiocytes stained weakly; controls had weak-to-moderate uniform staining. Cardiocyte staining intensity was significantly higher in IDCM, while vascular and interstitial-cell staining was similar between groups.

The authors interpret the heterogeneous myocardial BRCA1 pattern as reflecting adverse-remodeling biology: relatively low BRCA1 in dysfunctional cardiomyocytes could imply lower anti-apoptotic and DNA-repair activity, with higher BRCA1 in hypertrophied fibers. This is an association/biological interpretation, not proof that BRCA1 causes remodeling or predicts future remodeling.
